## Study Design, Biomedical Cohorts, and Synthetic Ground-Truth Regimes

We evaluate the `{python} N.n_models_word` benchmarked architectures defined in Chapter 2 across `{python} N.n_blocks` multi-view benchmarks: six real biomedical and clinical cohorts (`ADNI-MCI`, `MultiOmics` [TCGA-BRCA], `TCGA-KIRC`, `Heart`, `Diabetes`, and `mfeat`) and six synthetic generative regimes with known ground-truth latent coordinates $\mathbf{U}^*$ and feature supports $\mathbf{V}_m^*$ (@tbl-benchmark-cohorts). Every model is evaluated across `{python} N.n_seeds` independent 70/30 stratified or random train/test splits (seeds $42, 43, 44$) across three `nsa_flow` quantile sparsity levels ($q \in \{\text{None}, 0.5, 0.8\}$, `{python} N.n_default_fits` train/test fits), plus `{python} N.n_positive_reruns` paired reruns with non-negative loadings on the three high-dimensional cohorts and a `{python} N.sweep_n`-configuration hyperparameter sweep on `ADNI-MCI` ($N = 1,084$, one seed). To prevent data leakage, all feature standardization (`StandardScaler`), column completeness filtering ($\ge 98\%$), and demographic covariate adjustments (Frisch–Waugh–Lovell residualization [@frisch1933partial; @lovell1963seasonal] of age, biological sex, and education inside `ADNI-MCI`) are fitted strictly within each training split and applied out-of-sample to the held-out test split.

import os
import pandas as pd
from tabulate import tabulate

csv_path = "results_cache/deep_ranking_benchmark.csv"
if not os.path.exists(csv_path):
    csv_path = "paper/results_cache/deep_ranking_benchmark.csv"

df = pd.read_csv(csv_path)
df["Model"] = df["Model"].replace({"Flow-SiMLR-V": "Flow-SiMR-V", "Flow-SiMLR": "Flow-SiMR"})

cohort_meta = [
    ("ADNI-MCI", "Clinical MRI + Cog", 1084, "4 [160, 160, 62, 11]", "CogPC1 R2 (MRI Only)"),
    ("MultiOmics (BRCA)", "Oncology (mRNA/CNV/RPPA)", 822, "3 [200, 150, 150]", "ER Status Accuracy"),
    ("TCGA-KIRC", "Oncology (mRNA/CNV/RPPA)", 467, "3 [200, 150, 150]", "Pathologic Stage Acc"),
    ("Diabetes", "Clinical Chemistries", 442, "2 [5, 5]", "1-Yr Progression R2"),
    ("Heart", "Cardiology Vitals + ECG", 297, "2 [7, 6]", "Coronary Disease Acc"),
    ("mfeat", "Multi-Descriptor Digits", 2000, "4 [76, 64, 6, 47]", "10-Class Accuracy"),
    ("Linear", "Synthetic (50% Sparse ±)", 1000, "3 [100, 80, 60]", "Latent R2 & Support F1"),
    ("Polynomial", "Synthetic (Deg-3 Warped)", 1000, "3 [120, 80, 50]", "Latent R2 & CMC"),
    ("Sine", "Synthetic (Harmonic Warp)", 1000, "3 [120, 80, 50]", "Latent R2 & CMC"),
    ("Shared+Private", "Synthetic (80% Sparse ±)", 1000, "3 [160, 60, 30]", "Latent R2 & Support F1"),
    ("NonnegParts", "Synthetic (66.7% Non-Neg)", 400, "3 [120, 45, 30]", "Dominant Factor R2 & F1"),
    ("NonnegWeak", "Synthetic (80% Non-Neg)", 400, "3 [120, 45, 30]", "Weak Factor u3 R2 & F1"),
]

rows = []
for ds_label, domain, n_subj, views_str, task_str in cohort_meta:
    if "MultiOmics" in ds_label:
        ds_key = "MultiOmics"
    elif ds_label == "NonnegWeak":
        ds_key = "NonnegPartsWeak"
    else:
        ds_key = ds_label
    sub = df[df["Dataset"] == ds_key]
    agg_xv = sub.groupby("Model")["Strictly_Linear_Metric"].mean()
    pca_v = agg_xv["PCA"]
    best_m = agg_xv.idxmax()
    best_v = agg_xv.max()
    rows.append([
        ds_label,
        domain,
        f"{n_subj:,}",
        views_str,
        task_str,
        f"{best_m} ({best_v:.3f} vs PCA {pca_v:.3f})"
    ])

headers = ["Cohort", "Domain / Modality Structure", "N", "Views [p_m]", "Clinical / Task Target", "Best Linear XV vs PCA"]
print(tabulate(rows, headers=headers, tablefmt="pipe", disable_numparse=True, colalign=("left", "left", "right", "left", "left", "left")))
```

In `ADNI-MCI` ($N = 1,084$) [@mueller2005; @jack2008alzheimer; @ADNI], Views 0–2 capture $382$ regional structural MRI features from the ANTsPyT1w/ANTsPyMM pipelines: the volumes of 160 hierarchical segmentation labels (View 0: cortical, subcortical, ventricular, white-matter and cerebellar labels), the volume-to-surface-area ratio of the same 160 labels (View 1; for a cortical label it tracks thickness, otherwise it is a shape index), and DiReCT cortical thickness averaged in each of 62 Desikan–Killiany–Tourville (DKT) cortical regions (View 2) [@avants2008symmetric; @avants2011reproducible; @tustison2014large; @desikan2006automated; @klein2012mindboggle; @stone2020longitudinal; @stone2024blast; @Marek2011; @smith2013functional], while View 3 comprises eleven neuropsychological scales (`ADAS11`, `ADAS13`, `ADASQ4` [@rosen1984new], `MMSE` [@folstein1975mini], `CDRSB` [@morris1993clinical], `TRABSCOR` [@reitan1958validity], `FAQ` [@pfeffer1982measurement], and four Rey Auditory Verbal Learning Test sub-scores `RAVLT_immediate`, `RAVLT_learning`, `RAVLT_forgetting`, `RAVLT_perc_forgetting` [@rey1964examen]). Following `Protocol B`, the three MRI views align with the cognitive battery during training, but test-set predictions are generated exclusively from structural MRI. In `MultiOmics` (`TCGA-BRCA`, $N =$ `{python} n_brca_obs`) [@tcga2012breast] and `TCGA-KIRC` ($N = 467$) [@tcga2013kirc], mRNA expression ($p_1 = 200$), somatic copy-number variation ($p_2 = 150$), and RPPA proteomics ($p_3 = 150$) predict clinical Estrogen Receptor status and pathologic tumor stage, respectively.

## Global 12-Dataset Benchmark: Subspace Capacity vs. Single-Axis Interpretability

Across the $B =$ `{python} N.n_blocks` dataset blocks and `{python} N.n_models_word` architectures, block-averaged non-parametric Friedman [@friedman1937use] and Iman–Davenport [@Iman1980] omnibus tests differentiate the `{python} N.n_models_word` models on both the linear subspace probe ($\chi_F^2 =$ `{python} N.fr_lin_chi2`, $p =$ `{python} N.fr_lin_p`; $F_F =$ `{python} N.fr_lin_F`, $p =$ `{python} N.fr_lin_pF`) and the multi-modal consensus probe ($\chi_F^2 =$ `{python} N.fr_u_chi2`, $p =$ `{python} N.fr_u_p`; $F_F =$ `{python} N.fr_u_F`, $p =$ `{python} N.fr_u_pF`; Nemenyi Critical Difference $CD =$ `{python} N.cd` at $\alpha = 0.05$ [@Demsar2006; @Nemenyi1963; @benavoli2016should]). @tbl-global-leaderboard summarizes the global metrics across all `{python} N.n_models_word` models, accompanied by the Demšar Critical Difference diagram (@fig-cd-diagram), the multi-objective speed–accuracy and support–consensus Pareto frontiers (@fig-pareto-frontier), and the three-probe performance profile (@fig-three-probes).

import os
import sys
import pandas as pd
from tabulate import tabulate

csv_main = "results_cache/deep_ranking_benchmark.csv"
if not os.path.exists(csv_main):
    csv_main = "paper/results_cache/deep_ranking_benchmark.csv"

csv_op = "results_cache/operating_points_05_08_benchmark.csv"
if not os.path.exists(csv_op):
    csv_op = "paper/results_cache/operating_points_05_08_benchmark.csv"

df_main = pd.read_csv(csv_main)
df_main["Model"] = df_main["Model"].replace({"Flow-SiMLR-V": "Flow-SiMR-V", "Flow-SiMLR": "Flow-SiMR"})

from paper_numbers import op_default
df_op = op_default()  # default positivity only; the paired positive reruns would double-weight 3 cohorts
sub05 = df_op[df_op["Sparseness_Target"] == 0.5]

repo_root = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.getcwd(), "..")) if "paper" in os.getcwd() else os.getcwd()
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(repo_root, "src"))
from pysimlr.benchmarks.deep_ranking import build_ranking_blocks, friedman_test

piv_xv, _ = build_ranking_blocks(df_main, metric_col="Strictly_Linear_Metric", floor_threshold=None)
f_xv = friedman_test(piv_xv.values, higher_is_better=True)
ranks_xv = pd.Series(f_xv["mean_ranks"], index=piv_xv.columns)

syn_df = sub05[sub05["Case_Type"] == "synthetic"]
syn_f1 = syn_df.groupby("Model")["Support_Recovery_V"].mean()
syn_cmc = df_main[df_main["Case_Type"] == "synthetic"].groupby("Model")["CMC_Latent_U"].mean()

agg05 = sub05.groupby("Model").agg({
    "Strictly_Linear_Metric": "mean",
    "Axis_Sensitive_Metric": "mean",
    "Predictive_Metric": "mean",
    "Sparsity_Ratio": "mean",
    "Fit_Seconds": "mean"
})

order = ranks_xv.sort_values().index.tolist()
rows = []
for m in order:
    lin_v = agg05.loc[m, "Strictly_Linear_Metric"]
    rf_v = agg05.loc[m, "Axis_Sensitive_Metric"]
    u_v = agg05.loc[m, "Predictive_Metric"]
    drop_v = rf_v - lin_v
    rows.append([
        m,
        f"{ranks_xv[m]:.2f}",
        f"{lin_v:.3f}",
        f"{rf_v:.3f} ({drop_v:+.3f})",
        f"{u_v:.3f}",
        f"{syn_cmc[m]:.3f}",
        f"{syn_f1[m]:.3f}",
        f"{agg05.loc[m, 'Sparsity_Ratio']*100:.1f}"
    ])

headers = [
    "Architecture", "Friedman Rank ↓", "Linear XV ↑", "RF Axis XV (Drop) ↑",
    "Consensus U ↑", "Latent CMC ↑", "Support F1 ↑", "Sparsity % ↑"
]
print(tabulate(rows, headers=headers, tablefmt="pipe", disable_numparse=True, colalign=("left", "right", "right", "right", "right", "right", "right", "right")))

#| warning: false

The horizontal axis plots mean Friedman rank (lower is better, $1 =$ best), horizontal bars connect cliques within the Nemenyi Critical Difference ($\\alpha = 0.05$), and green stars (`*`) mark architectures on the 5-objective non-dominated Pareto frontier."
#| out-width: 100%
#| echo: false
import os
import sys
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

csv_main = "results_cache/deep_ranking_benchmark.csv"
if not os.path.exists(csv_main):
    csv_main = "paper/results_cache/deep_ranking_benchmark.csv"

df_main = pd.read_csv(csv_main)
df_main["Model"] = df_main["Model"].replace({"Flow-SiMLR-V": "Flow-SiMR-V", "Flow-SiMLR": "Flow-SiMR"})

repo_root = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.getcwd(), "..")) if "paper" in os.getcwd() else os.getcwd()
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(repo_root, "src"))
from pysimlr.benchmarks.deep_ranking import build_ranking_blocks, friedman_test, compute_nemenyi_cd, compute_pareto_frontier
from pysimlr.plotting import theme, VIEW_COLORS

piv_xv, _ = build_ranking_blocks(df_main, metric_col="Strictly_Linear_Metric", floor_threshold=None)
f_xv = friedman_test(piv_xv.values, higher_is_better=True)
ranks = pd.Series(f_xv["mean_ranks"], index=piv_xv.columns).sort_values()
cd = compute_nemenyi_cd(piv_xv.shape[1], piv_xv.shape[0])

agg_all = df_main.groupby("Model", as_index=False).agg({
    "Predictive_Metric": "mean",
    "Strictly_Linear_Metric": "mean",
    "CMC_Latent_U": "mean",
    "Support_Recovery_V": "mean",
    "Fit_Seconds": "mean"
})
pareto_df = compute_pareto_frontier(
    agg_all,
    objectives=["Predictive_Metric", "Strictly_Linear_Metric", "CMC_Latent_U", "Support_Recovery_V", "Fit_Seconds"],
    maximize=[True, True, True, True, False]
)
pareto_set = set(pareto_df[pareto_df["is_pareto_optimal"]]["Model"])
n_m = len(ranks)

with theme():
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10.5, 3.6), dpi=300)
    ax.set_xlim(0.15, n_m + 0.85)
    ax.set_ylim(0.0, 1.25)
    ax.axis("off")

    # Number line 1..n_m
    y_axis = 0.92
    ax.plot([1, n_m], [y_axis, y_axis], color="#0b0b0b", lw=1.4)
    for r_tick in range(1, n_m + 1):
        ax.plot([r_tick, r_tick], [y_axis - 0.035, y_axis + 0.035], color="#0b0b0b", lw=1.1)
        ax.text(r_tick, y_axis + 0.06, str(r_tick), ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=9.5, weight="semibold", color="#0b0b0b")

    # Nemenyi CD reference bar at top left
    cd_x0 = 1.0
    cd_y = 1.15
    ax.plot([cd_x0, cd_x0 + cd], [cd_y, cd_y], color="#e34948", lw=2.2)
    ax.plot([cd_x0, cd_x0], [cd_y - 0.03, cd_y + 0.03], color="#e34948", lw=1.5)
    ax.plot([cd_x0 + cd, cd_x0 + cd], [cd_y - 0.03, cd_y + 0.03], color="#e34948", lw=1.5)
    ax.text(cd_x0 + cd / 2, cd_y + 0.035, f"Nemenyi CD = {cd:.2f} (α = 0.05)", ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=9.0, weight="semibold", color="#e34948")

    # Split models into left and right
    n_left = (n_m + 1) // 2
    left_models = list(ranks.index[:n_left])
    right_models = list(ranks.index[n_left:])

    y_positions_left = np.linspace(0.60, 0.12, len(left_models))
    for idx_m, m in enumerate(left_models):
        r_val = ranks[m]
        y_m = y_positions_left[idx_m]
        is_p = m in pareto_set
        col_m = "#0ca30c" if is_p else "#0b0b0b"
        star = " *" if is_p else ""
        ax.plot([r_val, r_val], [y_axis, y_m], color="#898781", lw=0.9, linestyle="-")
        ax.plot([r_val, 0.85], [y_m, y_m], color="#898781", lw=0.9, linestyle="-")
        ax.plot(r_val, y_axis, "o", color=col_m, markeredgecolor="#fcfcfb", markeredgewidth=1.2, markersize=7.0)
        ax.text(0.80, y_m, f"{m}{star} ({r_val:.2f})", ha="right", va="center", fontsize=9.0, weight="semibold", color=col_m)

    y_positions_right = np.linspace(0.60, 0.18, len(right_models))
    for idx_m, m in enumerate(right_models):
        r_val = ranks[m]
        y_m = y_positions_right[idx_m]
        is_p = m in pareto_set
        col_m = "#0ca30c" if is_p else "#0b0b0b"
        star = " *" if is_p else ""
        ax.plot([r_val, r_val], [y_axis, y_m], color="#898781", lw=0.9, linestyle="-")
        ax.plot([r_val, n_m + 0.15], [y_m, y_m], color="#898781", lw=0.9, linestyle="-")
        ax.plot(r_val, y_axis, "o", color=col_m, markeredgecolor="#fcfcfb", markeredgewidth=1.2, markersize=7.0)
        ax.text(n_m + 0.20, y_m, f"({r_val:.2f}) {m}{star}", ha="left", va="center", fontsize=9.0, weight="semibold", color=col_m)

    # Clique bars
    r_vals = ranks.values
    cliques = []
    for i in range(len(r_vals)):
        j = i
        while j + 1 < len(r_vals) and (r_vals[j + 1] - r_vals[i]) <= cd:
            j += 1
        if j > i:
            is_sub = any(c_i <= i and j <= c_j for c_i, c_j in cliques)
            if not is_sub:
                cliques.append((i, j))

    clique_y_base = 0.81
    for c_idx, (i, j) in enumerate(cliques):
        cy = clique_y_base - c_idx * 0.065
        ax.plot([r_vals[i], r_vals[j]], [cy, cy], color="#0b0b0b", lw=3.6, solid_capstyle="round")

    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
```

#| out-width: 100%
#| echo: false
import os
import sys
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

csv_main = "results_cache/deep_ranking_benchmark.csv"
if not os.path.exists(csv_main):
    csv_main = "paper/results_cache/deep_ranking_benchmark.csv"

df_main = pd.read_csv(csv_main)
df_main["Model"] = df_main["Model"].replace({"Flow-SiMLR-V": "Flow-SiMR-V", "Flow-SiMLR": "Flow-SiMR"})

repo_root = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.getcwd(), "..")) if "paper" in os.getcwd() else os.getcwd()
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(repo_root, "src"))
from pysimlr.benchmarks.deep_ranking import compute_pareto_frontier
from pysimlr.plotting import theme, VIEW_COLORS

agg_all = df_main.groupby("Model", as_index=False).agg({
    "Predictive_Metric": "mean",
    "Strictly_Linear_Metric": "mean",
    "CMC_Latent_U": "mean",
    "Support_Recovery_V": "mean",
    "Fit_Seconds": "mean"
})
p_df = compute_pareto_frontier(
    agg_all,
    objectives=["Predictive_Metric", "Strictly_Linear_Metric", "CMC_Latent_U", "Support_Recovery_V", "Fit_Seconds"],
    maximize=[True, True, True, True, False]
).set_index("Model")
syn_sub = df_main[df_main["Case_Type"] == "synthetic"].groupby("Model")[["CMC_Latent_U", "Support_Recovery_V"]].mean()

with theme():
    fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11.2, 4.3), dpi=300, constrained_layout=True)

    # Panel A: Consensus U vs Fit_Seconds
    for m, row in p_df.iterrows():
        is_p = bool(row["is_pareto_optimal"])
        marker = "*" if is_p else "o"
        sz = 150 if is_p else 75
        col = "#0ca30c" if is_p else VIEW_COLORS[0]
        ax1.scatter(row["Fit_Seconds"], row["Predictive_Metric"], marker=marker, s=sz, color=col, edgecolor="#fcfcfb", lw=1.2, zorder=4)

    offsets_a = {
        "PCA": (-10, -14),
        "NSAFlow-PCA": (9, 4),
        "SiMLR": (-42, -2),
        "LEND": (-18, 9),
        "NED": (-34, -4),
        "NEDPP": (-44, -3),
        "Flow-SiMR-V": (-34, 9),
    }
    for m, row in p_df.iterrows():
        dx, dy = offsets_a.get(m, (6, 4))
        col_t = "#0b0b0b" if row["is_pareto_optimal"] else "#52514e"
        ax1.annotate(m, (row["Fit_Seconds"], row["Predictive_Metric"]), xytext=(dx, dy), textcoords="offset points", fontsize=8.4, weight="semibold", color=col_t)

    front_a = p_df.loc[RAW["pareto_2d_models"]]
    ax1.plot(front_a["Fit_Seconds"], front_a["Predictive_Metric"], "--", color="#0ca30c", lw=1.6, alpha=0.85, label="2D Speed–Accuracy Envelope")

    ax1.set_xscale("log")
    ax1.set_xlim(0.005, 35.0)
    ax1.set_ylim(0.61, 0.765)
    ax1.set_xlabel(r"Mean Fit Time in Seconds (Log Scale, $\downarrow$ Faster)")
    ax1.set_ylabel(r"Out-of-Sample Consensus Score (U $\uparrow$)")
    ax1.set_title("A. Consensus Accuracy vs. Fit Time")
    ax1.grid(True)
    ax1.legend(loc="lower left")

    # Panel B: Support F1 vs CMC on Synthetic Regimes
    for m in syn_sub.index:
        is_p = bool(p_df.loc[m, "is_pareto_optimal"])
        marker = "*" if is_p else "o"
        sz = 150 if is_p else 75
        col = "#0ca30c" if is_p else VIEW_COLORS[0]
        ax2.scatter(syn_sub.loc[m, "CMC_Latent_U"], syn_sub.loc[m, "Support_Recovery_V"], marker=marker, s=sz, color=col, edgecolor="#fcfcfb", lw=1.2, zorder=4)

    offsets_b = {
        "PCA": (9, -3),
        "NSAFlow-PCA": (-80, 5),
        "NEDPP": (-44, -12),
        "NED": (7, -12),
        "LEND": (-38, 6),
        "Flow-SiMR-V": (-26, 10),
        "SiMLR": (-36, -15),
    }
    for m in syn_sub.index:
        dx, dy = offsets_b.get(m, (6, 4))
        col_t = "#0b0b0b" if p_df.loc[m, "is_pareto_optimal"] else "#52514e"
        ax2.annotate(m, (syn_sub.loc[m, "CMC_Latent_U"], syn_sub.loc[m, "Support_Recovery_V"]), xytext=(dx, dy), textcoords="offset points", fontsize=8.4, weight="semibold", color=col_t)

    ax2.set_xlim(0.32, 0.95)
    ax2.set_ylim(-0.04, 0.74)

Three empirical principles emerge from @tbl-global-leaderboard and Figures [-@fig-cd-diagram]–[-@fig-three-probes]:

1. **Multi-View Alignment Against Single-Matrix Factorization**: The leading mean Friedman ranks on the linear entrypoint probe are `{python} N.rank_lin_top4`, against `PCA` (`{python} N.rank_lin_PCA`) and `NSAFlow-PCA` (`{python} N.rank_lin_NSAFlow_PCA`) (@fig-benchmark-uncertainty). On heterogeneous cohorts such as `mfeat` ($p = [76, 64, 6, 47]$) and `Shared+Private` ($p = [160, 60, 30]$), concatenated `PCA` reaches a linear score of `{python} N.mfeat_pca` (`mfeat` accuracy) and `{python} N.sp_pca` (`Shared+Private` $R^2$), against `{python} N.mfeat_best` (`{python} N.mfeat_best_model`) and `{python} N.sp_best` (`{python} N.sp_best_model`) for the best multi-view model. Over the `{python} N.n_blocks` datasets (seeds averaged, Wilcoxon signed-rank against `PCA` with Holm adjustment, @sec-app-operational), the linear score differs from `PCA` at $p < 0.05$ for `{python} N.wilcoxon_n_sig` of `{python} n_non_pca` `{python} wilcoxon_sig_phrase`.
2. **Coordinate Alignment and the Random Forest Axis Drop**: As established in @eq-subspace-invariance, ridge regression on $\mathbf{X}_m \mathbf{V}_m$ is insensitive to orthogonal or oblique column mixing $\mathbf{V}_m \mathbf{M}$, hiding the fact that dense `PCA` mixes distinct mechanisms across columns. With coordinate-splitting decision trees (`RandomForest`), `PCA` loses `{python} N.drop_pca` on average across the `{python} N.n_blocks` cohorts (Random Forest minus linear score), falling from `{python} N.npw_pca` to `{python} N.npw_pca_rf` on the weak sparse factors of `NonnegPartsWeak` and from `{python} N.adni_pca` to `{python} N.adni_pca_rf` on `ADNI-MCI` (`{python} N.adni_pca_rf_drop_pct` lower). The smallest drops are `{python} N.drop_best_models`.
3. **Operating Points and Feature Density ($q = 0.5$ vs. $q = 0.8$)**: @fig-operating-point-and-support shows the quantile threshold $q$ as a lens on feature support recovery without conflating scales on secondary axes. Across the `{python} N.n_default_fits` default-positivity fits, the mean linear score is `{python} N.op_lin_None`, `{python} N.op_lin_05` and `{python} N.op_lin_08` at $q = \text{None}$, $0.5$ and $0.8$, and the mean Random Forest axis score is `{python} N.op_rf_None`, `{python} N.op_rf_05` and `{python} N.op_rf_08`; at $q = 0.8$, `{python} N.op_sparsity_08` of loadings are zero while `{python} N.op_retained_08` of the best linear score is retained. At $q = 0.5$, support recovery on the $50\%$-sparse `Linear` regime ranges from $F_1 =$ `{python} N.f1_linear_q05_min` (`{python} N.f1_linear_q05_min_model`) to `{python} N.f1_linear_q05_max` (`{python} N.f1_linear_q05_max_model`), and reaches `{python} N.f1_np_q05_best` on `NonnegParts` (`{python} N.f1_np_q05_best_model`). On the focal $20\%$-active modules, the best $F_1$ at $q = 0.8$ is `{python} N.f1_npw_q08_best` on `NonnegPartsWeak` (`{python} N.f1_npw_q08_best_model`) and `{python} N.f1_sp_q08_best` on `Shared+Private` (`{python} N.f1_sp_q08_best_model`).

## Non-Subtractive Sparsification and Two-Stage Uniform Shrinkage: Synthetic Verification (Propositions 1–3) {#sec-exp-synthetic-v043}

Numerical checks and 20-seed synthetic benchmarks verify Propositions 1–3 and two-stage support-restricted uniform shrinkage (`results_cache/v043_synthetic_theorems.json` from `scripts/benchmark_synthetic_theorems.py`; @sec-non-subtractive-sparsification; @sec-uniform-shrinkage; @donoho1994ideal).

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: false
import json, os, re
from IPython.display import Markdown
from paper_numbers import CACHE

with open(os.path.join(CACHE, "v043_synthetic_theorems.json")) as fh:
    _syn_meta = json.load(fh)

_mp1 = _syn_meta["propositions"]["prop1"]
_mp2 = _syn_meta["propositions"]["prop2"]
_mp3 = _syn_meta["propositions"]["prop3"]
_mda = _syn_meta["design_a_rank1_sparse"]["description"]
_mdb = _syn_meta["design_b_rank2_disjoint"]["description"]

_m_rho = re.search(r"rho=([0-9.]+)", _mda)
_m_act_a = re.search(r"(\d+%)\s+active", _mda)
_m_act_b = re.search(r"\((\d+%)\s*\+\s*(\d+%)\s+active", _mdb)
if _m_rho is None or _m_act_a is None or _m_act_b is None:
    raise ValueError("Unexpected description format in v043_synthetic_theorems.json")

syn_p1_p = Markdown(f"$p = {_mp1['p']}$")
syn_p1_q = Markdown(f"$q = {_mp1['q']:.2f}$")
syn_p1_pq = Markdown(f"$p = {_mp1['p']}, q = {_mp1['q']:.2f}$")
syn_p1_alpha_range = Markdown(f"$\\alpha \\in [{_mp1['alphas_tested'][0]:g}, {_mp1['alphas_tested'][-1]:.2f}]$")
syn_p1_alpha_last = Markdown(f"$\\alpha = {_mp1['soft_threshold_floor_erosion'][-1]['alpha']:.2f}$")
syn_p2_pm = Markdown(f"$p = {_mp2['p']}, m = {_mp2['m']}$")
syn_p2_cvx_p = Markdown(f"$p = {_mp2['convexify_defect_p']}$")
syn_p3_k = Markdown(f"$k = {len(_mp3['support_sizes'])}$")
syn_p3_sizes = Markdown(str(_mp3["support_sizes"]))
syn_p3_alpha_range = Markdown(f"$\\alpha \\in [{_mp3['alpha_sweep'][0]['alpha']:g}, {_mp3['alpha_sweep'][-1]['alpha']:g}]$")
syn_m_views = Markdown(f"$M = {len(_syn_meta['provenance']['view_dims'])}$")
syn_rho = Markdown(f"$\\rho = {_m_rho.group(1)}$")
syn_a_active_pct = Markdown(_m_act_a.group(1))
syn_b_mode_pct = Markdown(f"{_m_act_b.group(1)}/{_m_act_b.group(2)}")
```

1. **Proposition 1 (Subtractive Shrinkage Cancellation, @eq-prop1-cancellation):** Across shrinkage levels `{python} syn_p1_alpha_range` on `{python} syn_p1_p` coordinates at `{python} syn_p1_q`, order-statistic quantile soft-thresholding (`sparseness_alg="soft"`) yields maximum $\ell_\infty$ deviation `{python} N.syn_prop1_max_linf` from the $\alpha = 0$ support and weights, confirming exact $\alpha$-cancellation. Under uniform-shrunk coordinate floors, continuous pre-retraction soft-thresholding (`sparseness_type="soft"`, `_apply_soft_threshold_sparseness`) suffers floor erosion: at `{python} syn_p1_alpha_last`, the uniform floor reaches `{python} N.syn_prop1_soft_floor_a099` above the threshold $\tau =$ `{python} N.syn_prop1_soft_tau_a099`, pulling cosine similarity with $\alpha = 0$ down to `{python} N.syn_prop1_soft_cos_a099` (@fig-v043-propositions A).
2. **Proposition 2 (Exact Top-$m$ Cardinality and Radial Simplex Normalization, @eq-prop2-radial-simplex):** On `{python} syn_p2_pm`, exact cardinality-constrained projection preserves the Cauchy–Schwarz variance bound with absolute error `{python} N.syn_prop2_cs_err` and achieves lower Euclidean squared error (`{python} N.syn_prop2_euclid_exact` vs. `{python} N.syn_prop2_euclid_soft`) and higher cosine similarity (`{python} N.syn_prop2_cos_exact` vs. `{python} N.syn_prop2_cos_soft`) than shifted soft-thresholding. At `sparseness=None` (`{python} syn_p2_cvx_p`), legacy Euclidean simplex projection subtracts $\theta =$ `{python} N.syn_prop2_legacy_theta`, zeros `{python} N.syn_prop2_legacy_zeroed_pct` of active coordinates, and lowers cosine similarity with the input direction to `{python} N.syn_prop2_legacy_cos`, whereas radial simplex normalization retains cosine `{python} N.syn_prop2_radial_cos` with zero dropped coordinates (@fig-v043-propositions B).
3. **Proposition 3 (Column-Support Uniform Shrinkage Orthogonality, @eq-prop3-support-shrinkage):** On `{python} syn_p3_k` disjoint column supports of size `{python} syn_p3_sizes`, `ColumnSupportShrinkageOperator` maintains exact orthogonality across `{python} syn_p3_alpha_range` with maximum Gram Frobenius error `{python} N.syn_prop3_max_fro`, whereas global `UniformShrinkageOperator` mixes the supports until Frobenius error reaches `{python} N.syn_prop3_global_fro_a1` and column cosine reaches `{python} N.syn_prop3_global_cos_a1` at $\alpha = 1$ (@fig-v043-propositions C).

::: {#fig-v043-propositions}

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-width: 100%
#| echo: false
import json, os
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from paper_numbers import CACHE
from pysimlr.plotting import theme, VIEW_COLORS

with open(os.path.join(CACHE, "v043_synthetic_theorems.json")) as fh:
    _syn = json.load(fh)
_p1 = _syn["propositions"]["prop1"]
_p2 = _syn["propositions"]["prop2"]
_p3 = _syn["propositions"]["prop3"]

with theme():
    fig, (ax1, ax2, ax3) = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(13.2, 4.0), dpi=200, constrained_layout=True)

    # Panel A: Prop 1 floor erosion
    _fe = _p1["soft_threshold_floor_erosion"]
    _a1 = [r["alpha"] for r in _fe]
    ax1.plot(_a1, [r["cos_with_alpha0_quantile_soft"] for r in _fe], "o-", color=VIEW_COLORS[0], lw=2.0, label="Quantile soft (Prop 1)")
    ax1.plot(_a1, [r["cos_with_alpha0_soft_thresh"] for r in _fe], "s--", color=VIEW_COLORS[1], lw=2.0, label="Shifted soft-thresh")
    ax1.set_xlabel("Uniform shrinkage alpha")
    ax1.set_ylabel(r"Cosine with alpha = 0 ($\uparrow$)")
    ax1.set_title("A. Prop 1: alpha-cancellation")
    ax1.set_ylim(0.55, 1.04)
    ax1.grid(True)
    ax1.legend(loc="lower left", fontsize=8.0)

    # Panel B: Prop 2 radial vs legacy convexify and exact top-m
    _lbls = ["Exact top-m\ncosine", "Soft-thresh\ncosine", "Radial _convexify\ncosine", "Legacy _convexify\ncosine"]
    _vals = [
        _p2["cos_sim_exact_topk"],
        _p2["cos_sim_soft_thresh"],
        _p2["radial_convexify_cos_with_input"],
        _p2["legacy_convexify_cos_with_input"],
    ]
    _cols = [VIEW_COLORS[0], VIEW_COLORS[1], VIEW_COLORS[2], "#d03b3b"]
    _xb = np.arange(len(_lbls))
    _bars = ax2.bar(_xb, _vals, color=_cols, width=0.58)
    for _b in _bars:
        _h = _b.get_height()
        ax2.text(_b.get_x() + _b.get_width() / 2, _h + 0.015, f"{_h:.3f}", ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=7.8, color="#0b0b0b")
    ax2.set_xticks(_xb)
    ax2.set_xticklabels(_lbls, fontsize=7.8)
    ax2.set_ylim(0.0, 1.14)
    ax2.set_ylabel(r"Directional cosine similarity ($\uparrow$)")
    ax2.set_title("B. Prop 2: radial simplex & top-m")
    ax2.grid(True, axis="y")

    # Panel C: Prop 3 Frobenius error & cosine across alpha
    _sw = _p3["alpha_sweep"]
    _a3 = [r["alpha"] for r in _sw]
    ax3.plot(_a3, [r["col_support_fro_err"] for r in _sw], "o-", color=VIEW_COLORS[0], lw=2.0, label="Col-support Fro err")
    ax3.plot(_a3, [r["global_smoother_fro_err"] for r in _sw], "s--", color="#d03b3b", lw=2.0, label="Global Fro err")
    ax3.plot(_a3, [r["global_smoother_cos"] for r in _sw], "^:", color=VIEW_COLORS[1], lw=1.8, label="Global col cosine")
    ax3.set_xlabel("Uniform shrinkage alpha")
    ax3.set_ylabel(r"Orthogonality error / cosine ($\downarrow$)")

```

Numerical verification of Propositions 1–3 on `pysimlr v0.43.1` (`v043_synthetic_theorems.json`). (A) Cosine similarity with the $\alpha = 0$ weight vector across `{python} syn_p1_alpha_range` (`{python} syn_p1_pq`): order-statistic quantile soft-thresholding (`sparseness_alg="soft"`) cancels $\alpha$ exactly while continuous pre-retraction soft-thresholding (`sparseness_type="soft"`) degrades under the uniform shrinkage floor. (B) Comparison of exact top-$m$ vs. soft-threshold cosine (`{python} syn_p2_pm`) and legacy Euclidean vs. radial `_convexify` cosine/zeroing at `sparseness=None` (`{python} syn_p2_cvx_p`). (C) Gram orthogonality Frobenius error $\|\mathbf{V}^\top \mathbf{V} - \mathbf{I}_2\|_F$ and inter-column cosine across `{python} syn_p3_alpha_range` on disjoint `{python} syn_p3_sizes` supports: `ColumnSupportShrinkageOperator` holds exact zero error while global uniform shrinkage collapses to collinearity.
:::

We next evaluate two-stage support-restricted uniform shrinkage (`fit_uniform_shrunk`, Donoho–Johnstone Risk Inflation Criterion `ric` @eq-ric-dof vs. `plugin` shrinkage) across `{python} N.syn_n_seeds` seeds in a four-view generative setting (`{python} syn_m_views`, view dimensions `{python} N.syn_view_dims`, $N_{\text{train}} =$ `{python} N.syn_n_train`, $N_{\text{test}} =$ `{python} N.syn_n_test`, block-correlated noise `{python} syn_rho` in blocks of size $5$). Design A tests rank $k = 1$ with `{python} syn_a_active_pct` active positive signal per view (@tbl-v043-design-a); Design B tests rank $k = 2$ with disjoint `{python} syn_b_mode_pct` active supports per view (@tbl-v043-design-b; @fig-v043-design-ab).

        f"{_d['support_f1']['mean']:.3f} ± {_d['support_f1']['sd']:.3f}",
        f"{_d['weight_cos']['mean']:.3f}",
        f"{_d['active_frac']['mean']:.3f}",
    ])
print(tabulate(

    tablefmt="pipe",
    disable_numparse=True,

Across the `{python} N.syn_n_seeds` seeds in Design A ($k = 1$, two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank tests), two-stage conical shrinkage at $q = 0.5$ with plugin $\alpha$ achieves $R^2 =$ `{python} N.ts_a_q05_conical_plug_r2_pm` and $F_1 =$ `{python} N.ts_a_q05_conical_plug_f1_pm` against global uniform shrinkage (`{python} N.ts_a_global_conical_r2_pm`, $F_1 =$ `{python} N.ts_a_global_conical_f1_pm`; $\Delta R^2 =$ `{python} N.ts_a_delta_con_plug_vs_global_r2`, $p =$ `{python} N.ts_a_p_con_plug_vs_global_r2`; $\Delta F_1 =$ `{python} N.ts_a_delta_con_plug_vs_global_f1`, $p =$ `{python} N.ts_a_p_con_plug_vs_global_f1`) and exceeds legacy soft-thresholding (`{python} N.ts_a_legacy_soft_r2_pm`; $\Delta R^2 =$ `{python} N.ts_a_delta_con_plug_vs_soft_r2`, $p =$ `{python} N.ts_a_p_con_plug_vs_soft_r2`). Under theoretical RIC shrinkage at $q = 0.5$, two-stage conical attains $R^2 =$ `{python} N.ts_a_q05_conical_ric_r2_pm` and $F_1 =$ `{python} N.ts_a_q05_conical_ric_f1_pm` ($\Delta R^2 =$ `{python} N.ts_a_delta_con_ric_vs_global_r2`, $p =$ `{python} N.ts_a_p_con_ric_vs_global_r2`; $\Delta F_1 =$ `{python} N.ts_a_delta_con_ric_vs_global_f1`, $p =$ `{python} N.ts_a_p_con_ric_vs_global_f1`). Two-stage radial convex ($q = 0.5$, plugin) reaches $R^2 =$ `{python} N.ts_a_q05_rcvx_plug_r2_pm` and $F_1 =$ `{python} N.ts_a_q05_rcvx_plug_f1_pm` against legacy Euclidean convex (`{python} N.ts_a_legacy_ecvx_r2_pm`, $F_1 =$ `{python} N.ts_a_legacy_ecvx_f1_pm`; $\Delta R^2 =$ `{python} N.ts_a_delta_rcvx_plug_vs_ecvx_r2`, $p =$ `{python} N.ts_a_p_rcvx_plug_vs_ecvx_r2`; $\Delta F_1 =$ `{python} N.ts_a_delta_rcvx_plug_vs_ecvx_f1`, $p =$ `{python} N.ts_a_p_rcvx_plug_vs_ecvx_f1`).

In Design B ($k = 2$ disjoint supports), two-stage conical shrinkage ($q = 0.5$, RIC) achieves mean $R^2 =$ `{python} N.ts_b_q05_conical_ric_r2_pm` and $F_1 =$ `{python} N.ts_b_q05_conical_ric_f1_pm` with exact orthogonality (`fro =` `{python} N.ts_b_q05_conical_ric_fro`, `cos =` `{python} N.ts_b_q05_conical_ric_cos`), outperforming global uniform shrinkage (`{python} N.ts_b_legacy_global_r2_pm`, $F_1 =$ `{python} N.ts_b_legacy_global_f1_pm`, `fro =` `{python} N.ts_b_legacy_global_fro`; $\Delta R^2 =$ `{python} N.ts_b_delta_con_ric_vs_global_r2`, $p =$ `{python} N.ts_b_p_con_ric_vs_global_r2`; $\Delta F_1 =$ `{python} N.ts_b_delta_con_ric_vs_global_f1`, $p =$ `{python} N.ts_b_p_con_ric_vs_global_f1`; $\Delta \text{Fro} =$ `{python} N.ts_b_delta_con_ric_vs_global_fro`, $p =$ `{python} N.ts_b_p_con_ric_vs_global_fro`) and legacy conical hard thresholding (`{python} N.ts_b_legacy_hard_r2_pm`, $F_1 =$ `{python} N.ts_b_legacy_hard_f1_pm`, `fro =` `{python} N.ts_b_legacy_hard_fro`; $\Delta R^2 =$ `{python} N.ts_b_delta_con_ric_vs_hard_r2`, $p =$ `{python} N.ts_b_p_con_ric_vs_hard_r2`; $\Delta F_1 =$ `{python} N.ts_b_delta_con_ric_vs_hard_f1`, $p =$ `{python} N.ts_b_p_con_ric_vs_hard_f1`). Two-stage radial convex ($q = 0.5$, RIC) attains $R^2 =$ `{python} N.ts_b_q05_rcvx_ric_r2_pm` and $F_1 =$ `{python} N.ts_b_q05_rcvx_ric_f1_pm` (`fro =` `{python} N.ts_b_q05_rcvx_ric_fro`), improving over legacy Euclidean convex (`{python} N.ts_b_legacy_ecvx_r2_pm`, $F_1 =$ `{python} N.ts_b_legacy_ecvx_f1_pm`, `fro =` `{python} N.ts_b_legacy_ecvx_fro`; $\Delta R^2 =$ `{python} N.ts_b_delta_rcvx_ric_vs_ecvx_r2`, $p =$ `{python} N.ts_b_p_rcvx_ric_vs_ecvx_r2`; $\Delta F_1 =$ `{python} N.ts_b_delta_rcvx_ric_vs_ecvx_f1`, $p =$ `{python} N.ts_b_p_rcvx_ric_vs_ecvx_f1`).

## Clinical Neuroimaging in `ADNI-MCI` ($N = 1,084$): Predicting Cognition from MRI Alone and Attributing the Prediction

A primary clinical test of multi-modal representation learning is whether aligning structural neuroimaging with multi-domain cognitive batteries during training yields an anatomical basis that better predicts cognitive severity in new patients who have only undergone an MRI scan (`Protocol B`). Across $N = 1,084$ participants with Mild Cognitive Impairment, @tbl-adni-mci-summary compares all `{python} N.n_models_word` benchmark models on held-out MRI-only prediction of composite cognitive impairment (`CogPC1` $R^2$, after in-fold adjustment for age, sex, and education), single-axis Random Forest prediction, and mean ridge regression $R^2$ across all eleven individual neuropsychological scales (`ADAS11`, `ADAS13`, `ADASQ4`, `MMSE`, `CDRSB`, `TRABSCOR`, `FAQ`, and four `RAVLT` memory scales).

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| label: tbl-adni-mci-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Out-of-sample MRI-only prediction of cognitive impairment on `ADNI-MCI` ($N = 1,084$, `Protocol B`: training alignment between 3 MRI views and 11 cognitive scales; cognitive views withheld at test time). 3-seed means $\\pm$ SD across seeds from the benchmark ($q = 0.5$, default positivity) alongside the best configuration per model in the single-seed hyperparameter sweep."
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
import os
import pandas as pd
from tabulate import tabulate

csv_op = "results_cache/operating_points_05_08_benchmark.csv"
if not os.path.exists(csv_op):
    csv_op = "paper/results_cache/operating_points_05_08_benchmark.csv"

csv_sw = "results_cache/adni_mci_1214_grid_sweep.csv"
if not os.path.exists(csv_sw):
    csv_sw = "paper/results_cache/adni_mci_1214_grid_sweep.csv"

from paper_numbers import op_default
df_op = op_default()  # default positivity only: 3 rows (seeds) per model
sub_adni = df_op[(df_op["Dataset"] == "ADNI-MCI") & (df_op["Sparseness_Target"] == 0.5)]

df_sw = pd.read_csv(csv_sw)
df_sw["Model"] = df_sw["Model"].replace({"Flow-SiMLR-V": "Flow-SiMR-V"})
df_sw_ok = df_sw[df_sw["Status"] == "ok"]
best_sw = df_sw_ok.sort_values("CogPC1_R2", ascending=False).groupby("Model", as_index=False).first().set_index("Model")

agg = sub_adni.groupby("Model").agg({
    "Strictly_Linear_Metric": ["mean", "std"],
    "Axis_Sensitive_Metric": "mean",
    "Predictive_Metric": "mean",
    "Sparsity_Ratio": "mean",
    "Frame_Defect_D": "mean"
})

order = agg[("Strictly_Linear_Metric", "mean")].sort_values(ascending=False).index.tolist()
rows = []
for m in order:
    lin_m = agg.loc[m, ("Strictly_Linear_Metric", "mean")]
    lin_s = agg.loc[m, ("Strictly_Linear_Metric", "std")]
    rf_m = agg.loc[m, ("Axis_Sensitive_Metric", "mean")]
    u_m = agg.loc[m, ("Predictive_Metric", "mean")]
    sp_m = agg.loc[m, ("Sparsity_Ratio", "mean")] * 100.0
    sw_r2 = best_sw.loc[m, "CogPC1_R2"] if m in best_sw.index else float("nan")
    sw_11 = best_sw.loc[m, "Mean11_RidgeCV"] if m in best_sw.index else float("nan")
    rows.append([
        m,
        f"{lin_m:.3f} ± {lin_s:.3f}",
        f"{rf_m:.3f}",
        f"{u_m:.3f}",
        f"{sw_r2:.3f}",
        f"{sw_11:.3f}",
        f"{sp_m:.1f}"
    ])

headers = [
    "Architecture", "3-Seed MRI Linear R2 ↑", "MRI RF Axis R2 ↑",
    "MRI Consensus R2 ↑", "Sweep Peak CogPC1 R2 ↑", "11-Scale Mean R2 ↑", "MRI Sparsity % ↑"
]
print(tabulate(rows, headers=headers, tablefmt="pipe", disable_numparse=True, colalign=("left", "right", "right", "right", "right", "right", "right")))
```

Comparing the unsupervised anatomical baselines against cognitive-aligned SiMR models in @tbl-adni-mci-summary and Figures [-@fig-adni-view-chord]–[-@fig-adni-scores] yields four findings:

1. **Supervising MRI Factor Discovery with Cognitive Batteries Improves Out-of-Sample MRI Prediction**: Unsupervised `PCA` on the $382$ structural MRI features explains $R^2 =$ `{python} N.adni_pca` $\pm$ `{python} N.adni_pca_sd` of out-of-sample cognitive variance (`CogPC1`) on the linear probe and `{python} N.adni_pca_rf` on the single-axis Random Forest probe. Aligning the MRI projections with the 11-scale cognitive battery during training gives, for the four leading models (3-seed means $\pm$ SD), `{python} N.adni_ranked`; the best is `{python} N.adni_gain_pct` over `PCA`. The best single-axis Random Forest score is `{python} N.adni_rf_best` (`{python} N.adni_rf_best_model`), `{python} N.adni_rf_ratio` times that of `PCA`. In the single-seed sweep the best configuration reaches `{python} N.sweep_best_r2` (`{python} N.sweep_best_model`) and the best linear-family configuration `{python} N.sweep_linear_best_r2` (`{python} N.sweep_linear_best_model`), against `{python} N.sweep_pca_r2` for `PCA`; mean prediction across all eleven scales reaches `{python} N.sweep_m11_best` (`{python} N.sweep_m11_best_model`) against `{python} N.sweep_m11_pca` for `PCA` (`{python} N.sweep_m11_gain`). These sweep peaks are maxima over many configurations on one split and are optimistic.
2. **Which MRI Features Carry the Prediction**: @fig-adni-neuroanatomy-flagship attributes the held-out `CogPC1` prediction of the non-negative $q = 0.85$ fit (all nine MRI columns, $R^2 =$ `{python} N.attr_full_r2`). One column per MRI view carries it. Alone, the predictive column gives $R^2 =$ `{python} N.attr_vol_best_r2` in volume (component `{python} N.attr_vol_best_c`), `{python} N.attr_va_best_r2` in vol/area (component `{python} N.attr_va_best_c`) and `{python} N.attr_dkt_best_r2` in DiReCT thickness (component `{python} N.attr_dkt_best_c`, `{python} N.attr_dkt_best_n` region), against at most `{python} N.attr_other_max_r2` for any other column, and only the vol/area column is not redundant with the rest (unique $R^2$ `{python} N.attr_va_best_unique`). Component numbers are not identifiable across fits, so the refits below follow each view's predictive column rather than a fixed index. Across `{python} N.attr_n_halves` half-sample refits, the predictive vol/area basis selects these features in at least half of them (fraction of refits): `{python} N.attr_cur_va_top`. These are mostly entorhinal, temporal-lobe and inferior parietal measures, the regions where atrophy is expected in prodromal Alzheimer's disease [@dickerson2009cortical; @jack2018nia]. DiReCT thickness tells the same story less clearly. Its first principal component explains `{python} N.attr_dkt_pc1` of the variance across the 62 regions (mean inter-region correlation `{python} N.attr_dkt_mean_corr`), and consensus component `{python} N.attr_global_c` correlates `{python} N.attr_global_r` with subject-mean thickness, so hard-assigning each region to its largest structure coefficient places `{python} N.attr_hard_counts` regions on components 1 / 2 / 3: a display of the global factor, not of localisation (Panel B). The thickness basis itself is unstable under the default collapse penalty: it keeps two or fewer regions in `{python} N.attr_cur_dkt_degenerate` of `{python} N.attr_n_halves` refits (median held-out $R^2$ `{python} N.attr_cur_dkt_med_r2`). Non-negative region sums on positively correlated features typically correlate above the penalty's threshold of 0.3, so the penalty pushes those columns towards one or two regions. With `collapse_weight = 0` the predictive thickness basis keeps a median of `{python} N.attr_nc_dkt_med_n` regions (two or fewer in `{python} N.attr_nc_dkt_degenerate` refit), its median $R^2$ rises to `{python} N.attr_nc_dkt_med_r2`, and its most frequent regions are (fraction of refits) `{python} N.attr_nc_dkt_top` (Panel D). No single thickness region replicates in more than `{python} N.attr_nc_dkt_top_max` of refits, so the thickness map is a pattern, not a list of identified regions (`docs/audit/evidence/adni_global_factor_check.csv`). For reference, unthresholded non-negative fits are `{python} N.fl_col_pca_simr_sp` sparse on the DKT view without rotation and `{python} N.fl_varimax_simr_sp` with Varimax, against `{python} N.fl_pca_sp` for dense `PCA`.
3. **Support-Shuffled and PCA-Rotated Score Controls**: To separate coordinate-level axis alignment and anatomical support localization from subspace capacity, two negative controls are evaluated across `{python} N.n_seeds` seeds on `ADNI-MCI` (`adni_mci_axis_alignment_controls.csv`, `axis_alignment_control_metrics`): (i) a PCA-rotated score control rotates the learned scores $\mathbf{Z} = [\mathbf{X}_m \mathbf{V}_m]$ by their in-fold principal-component eigenvectors, which leaves the linear probe unchanged (largest difference `{python} N.ctl_linear_invariance`) and lowers the single-axis Random Forest score for `{python} N.ctl_rot_n_lower` of `{python} N.ctl_n_models` models; (ii) a support-shuffled basis control permutes the rows of each $\mathbf{V}_m$ within its view, preserving sparsity, weight magnitudes and $\mathbf{V}_m^\top \mathbf{V}_m$, and lowers the Random Forest `CogPC1` $R^2$ for `{python} N.ctl_shuffle_n_lower` of `{python} N.ctl_n_models` models: `{python} N.ctl_shuffle_lowers`. Unshuffled Random Forest scores are `{python} N.ctl_rf_ratio_min` to `{python} N.ctl_rf_ratio_max` times that of `PCA`.
4. **Rank Selection, Component Identifiability, and Display Policy**: Evaluating latent rank selection via `select_rank(..., criterion="latent_reliability")` (@sec-stability-bagging-sem; @eq-oob-icc1) across 20 half-sample refits (`docs/audit/evidence/adni_rank_selection.csv`, selection margin `{python} N.adni_rank_margin`) selects $k =$ `{python} N.adni_pos_selected_k` under non-negative estimation (`positivity="positive"`) and $k =$ `{python} N.adni_either_selected_k` under signed estimation (`positivity="either"`). At $k = 2$ under non-negativity, out-of-bag univariate latent reliabilities are `{python} N.adni_k2_pos_rel_c1` and `{python} N.adni_k2_pos_rel_c2` (gains `{python} N.adni_k2_pos_gain_c1` and `{python} N.adni_k2_pos_gain_c2`), multivariate reliability is `{python} N.adni_k2_pos_mv_rel` (gain `{python} N.adni_k2_pos_mv_gain`), and `all_coupled =` `{python} N.adni_k2_pos_all_coupled` (`passed =` `{python} N.adni_k2_pos_passed`). At $k = 3$ under non-negativity, univariate reliabilities are `{python} N.adni_k3_pos_rel_c1`, `{python} N.adni_k3_pos_rel_c2`, and `{python} N.adni_k3_pos_rel_c3` (gains `{python} N.adni_k3_pos_gain_c1`, `{python} N.adni_k3_pos_gain_c2`, and `{python} N.adni_k3_pos_gain_c3`): Component 2 drops to minimum reliability `{python} N.adni_k3_pos_min_rel` (gain `{python} N.adni_k3_pos_min_gain`), multivariate reliability drops to `{python} N.adni_k3_pos_mv_rel` (gain declines from `{python} N.adni_k2_pos_mv_gain` at $k = 2$ to `{python} N.adni_k3_pos_mv_gain`, failing multivariate monotonicity), and `all_coupled =` `{python} N.adni_k3_pos_all_coupled` (`passed =` `{python} N.adni_k3_pos_passed`), so the fixed $k = 3$ diagnostic fits below isolate Components 1 and 3 as the two high-reliability axes. Under signed estimation (`positivity="either"`), $k = 2$ achieves reliabilities `{python} N.adni_k2_either_rel_c1` and `{python} N.adni_k2_either_rel_c2` (multivariate gain `{python} N.adni_k2_either_mv_gain`, `passed =` `{python} N.adni_k2_either_passed`), whereas at $k = 3$ reliabilities drop to `{python} N.adni_k3_either_rel_c1`, `{python} N.adni_k3_either_rel_c2`, and `{python} N.adni_k3_either_rel_c3` (minimum gain `{python} N.adni_k3_either_min_gain`, multivariate gain `{python} N.adni_k3_either_mv_gain`, `passed =` `{python} N.adni_k3_either_passed`).
   * **Signed Displays Protocol**: Across all displays in this manuscript: (i) feature maps display only features whose 95% bootstrap confidence interval (from whole-pipeline refits in `loading_inference`) strictly excludes zero; (ii) named biomarker panels report features selected via Meinshausen–Bühlmann stability selection at threshold $\pi_{\text{thr}} = 0.80$ with expected false selections $E[\text{false}] \le 1.0$; and (iii) non-negative displays present hard-assignment OLEE loadings accompanied by the `loading_margin` certainty metric.

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pysimlr

def _dkt_lobe(nm):
    s = nm.replace("left_", "").replace("right_", "")
    if any(k in s for k in ("entorhinal", "fusiform", "parahippocampal", "temporal")):
        return "Temporal"
    if any(k in s for k in ("cingulate",)):
        return "Cingulate"
    if any(k in s for k in ("parietal", "precuneus", "supramarginal", "postcentral")):
        return "Parietal"
    if any(k in s for k in ("cuneus", "occipital", "lingual", "pericalcarine")):
        return "Occipital"
    if "insula" in s:
        return "Insula"
    return "Frontal"

_dkt_groups = [_dkt_lobe(nm) for nm in _d_adni["names"][2]]
_all_adni_names = list(_d_adni["names"]) + [[f"cog_{i}" for i in range(_d_adni["y_tr"].shape[1])]]
fig = pysimlr.plot_feature_groups(
    _res_adni,
    _dkt_groups,
    view=2,
    feature_names=_all_adni_names,
    statistic="mean_abs",
    view_names=_adni_vnames,
)
plt.show()

```{python}
#| label: fig-nsa-v-interpretability
#| echo: false
#| out-width: 100%
#| fig-cap: "Sparse `LEND` OLEE loadings $\\mathbf{L}_m$ separate clinical feature blocks across `Heart` and `Diabetes` views with high Gini sparsity (`results_cache/nsa_v_loadings.json`). Heatmaps plot per-view loading matrices sorted by component assignment, reporting per-column Gini sparsity $G$ and mean winner-vs-runner-up loading margins."
import json, os
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from paper_numbers import CACHE
from pysimlr.plotting import theme, _cmap, _matrix, _header

with open(os.path.join(CACHE, "nsa_v_loadings.json")) as fh:
    NSAV = json.load(fh)

def _gini(x):
    x = np.sort(np.abs(np.asarray(x, float)))
    n = len(x)
    return 0.0 if x.sum() == 0 else float(np.sum((2 * np.arange(1, n + 1) - n - 1) * x) / (n * x.sum()))

with theme():
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(8.8, 8.6), dpi=300, layout="constrained")
    for ax, (cohort, view) in zip(axes.ravel(), [(c, v) for c in ("Heart", "Diabetes") for v in NSAV[c]]):
        d = NSAV[cohort][view]
        v = np.array(d.get("loadings", d.get("v")), float)
        margin = np.array(d["loading_margin"], float) if "loading_margin" in d and d["loading_margin"] is not None else None
        order = np.lexsort((-v.max(1), v.argmax(1), (v.max(1) <= 1e-4).astype(int)))
        v, rows = v[order], [d["rows"][i] for i in order]
        cols = [f"L{j + 1} (G={_gini(v[:, j]):.2f})" for j in range(v.shape[1])]
        _matrix(ax, v, _cmap("seq"), 0.0, 0.95, fmt="{:.2f}", rows=rows, cols=cols)
        margin_str = f" · margin {margin.mean():.2f}" if margin is not None else ""
        ax.set_title(f"{cohort}: {view}{margin_str}", loc="left", fontsize=9.8)
    _header(fig, "OLEE sparse basis loadings",
            "Gini sparsity G and mean winner-vs-runner-up loading margin per view")
    plt.show()
```

In `MultiOmics` (`TCGA-BRCA`, $N =$ `{python} n_brca_obs`), out-of-sample Estrogen Receptor classification accuracy on the linear entrypoint is `{python} N.brca_Flow_SiMR_V_pm` (`Flow-SiMR-V`), `{python} N.brca_LEND_pm` (`LEND`) and `{python} N.brca_NEDPP_pm` (`NEDPP`), against `{python} N.brca_PCA_pm` for `PCA` (3-seed means $\pm$ SD); the sparse non-negative dictionaries $\mathbf{V}_m$, tri-modal feature chord, and view-level quality radar are examined in @sec-app-brca. In `TCGA-KIRC` ($N = 467$), pathologic stage classification on the consensus embedding $\mathbf{U}$ is `{python} N.kirc_LEND_u_pm` for `LEND` against `{python} N.kirc_PCA_u_pm` for `PCA`. On compact clinical cohorts, `Diabetes` ($N =$ `{python} n_diab_obs`) reaches $R^2 =$ `{python} N.diab_SiMLR` for `SiMLR` against `{python} N.diab_pca` for `PCA`, and `Heart` ($N =$ `{python} n_heart_obs`) reaches accuracy `{python} N.heart_NSAFlow_PCA` for `NSAFlow-PCA` and `{python} N.heart_SiMLR` for `SiMLR`. @fig-diabetes-top-features, @fig-heart-audit, and @fig-nsa-v-interpretability show the stability-selected structure correlations, multi-view feature-to-component chord, and OLEE loadings $\mathbf{L}_m$ across `Heart` (out-of-bag `latent_reliability` `{python} heart_rel_c1` and `{python} heart_rel_c2`) and `Diabetes` (`latent_reliability` `{python} diab_rel_c1` and `{python} diab_rel_c2`); while the linear entrypoint $\mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}} = \mathbf{X}_m \mathbf{V}_m$ maps individual observations into the latent consensus space, the OLEE loadings $\mathbf{L}_m$ decompose individual patient profiles into exact additive risk attributions $c_{m,i,j,l} = x_{m,i,j} l_{m,j,l}$ without post-hoc Monte Carlo approximations [@Wachter_2017; @karimi2021algorithmic; @pearl2009causality]. Complete parameter sensitivity ablations (the $w \in [0.01, 0.95]$ trade-off curve, basis diagnostics, stability rank selection across $k$, and synthetic noise recovery) are in @sec-app-operational.

## Re-Benchmarking on Six Biomedical Cohorts (v0.43.1): Non-Subtractive Sparsification, Radial Simplex, and Uniform Shrinkage {#sec-exp-v043-revisit}

To measure the empirical impact of Propositions 1–3 on real biomedical cohorts (`pysimlr v0.43.1`, `scripts/run_real_data_v043.py`), we re-benchmark standard `simlr` (`Part A`) and evaluate two-stage uniform shrinkage `fit_uniform_shrunk` (`Part B`) across all six real cohorts (`ADNI-MCI`, `MultiOmics` [`TCGA-BRCA`], `TCGA-KIRC`, `Heart`, `Diabetes`, `mfeat`) over three random seeds (`42, 43, 44`).

In Part A (`part_a_comparison_summary.csv`, @tbl-v043-part-a), `{python} N.v043_n_conv` of `{python} N.v043_n_fits` `simlr` fits (`{python} N.v043_conv_pct`) converge; the single non-convergent run is `TCGA-KIRC` under `positivity="either"`, `sparseness=None`, seed `44` (`Stop_Reason = "max_iter"`). Across the `{python} N.v043_n_matched` matched fits (`{python} N.v043_n_matched_cells` cohort-by-positivity-by-sparseness cells $\times$ `{python} N.n_seeds` seeds) comparing `v0.43.1` against the pre-`v0.43` cache, signed `positivity="either"` improves mean consensus metric by `{python} N.v043_mean_either_delta` (`{python} N.v043_either_q05_mean_delta` at $q = 0.5$ and `{python} N.v043_either_q08_mean_delta` at $q = 0.8$), while non-negative `positivity="positive"` ranges from `{python} v043_min_pos_delta` to `{python} N.v043_max_pos_delta` ($\max |\Delta| =$ `{python} N.v043_pos_max_abs_delta`). Under radial simplex normalization (`positivity="convex"`) on the three high-dimensional biomedical cohorts, `MultiOmics` (`TCGA-BRCA`) reaches peak consensus accuracy `{python} N.v043_brca_cvx_best_u` and mean linear accuracy `{python} N.v043_brca_cvx_mean_lin` (mean consensus `{python} N.v043_brca_cvx_mean_u`), ahead of `positivity="positive"` (peak consensus `{python} N.v043_brca_pos_best_u`, mean linear `{python} N.v043_brca_pos_mean_lin`) and `positivity="either"` (peak consensus `{python} N.v043_brca_either_best_u`, mean linear `{python} N.v043_brca_either_mean_lin`).

import os
import pandas as pd
from tabulate import tabulate

csv_pa = "results_cache/part_a_comparison_summary.csv"
if not os.path.exists(csv_pa):
    csv_pa = "paper/results_cache/part_a_comparison_summary.csv"

df_pa = pd.read_csv(csv_pa)
rows_pa = []
for _, r in df_pa.iterrows():
    sp_k = "None" if pd.isna(r["Sparseness_Key"]) else f"{float(r['Sparseness_Key']):.1f}"
    cached_s = "--" if pd.isna(r["Cached_Metric"]) else f"{r['Cached_Metric']:.3f}"
    delta_s = "--" if pd.isna(r["Delta_Metric"]) else f"{r['Delta_Metric']:+.3f}"
    rows_pa.append([
        r["Dataset"],
        r["Positivity"],
        sp_k,
        f"{r['V043_Metric']:.3f}",
        f"{r['V043_Sparsity']*100:.1f}",
        f"{r['V043_Defect']:.4f}",
        f"{r['V043_Conv']:.2f}",
        cached_s,
        delta_s,
    ])
print(tabulate(
    rows_pa,
    headers=["Cohort", "Positivity", "q", "v0.43.1 U ↑", "Sparsity % ↑", "D(V) ↓", "Conv", "Pre-v0.43 U", "Δ U"],
    tablefmt="pipe",
    disable_numparse=True,
    colalign=("left", "left", "right", "right", "right", "right", "right", "right", "right"),
))
```

In Part B (`part_b_uniform_shrunk_summary.csv`, @tbl-v043-part-b; @fig-v043-real-revisit), we evaluate `{python} N.us_n_fits` `fit_uniform_shrunk` runs across all six cohorts and ranks $k \in \{1, 2, 3\}$ (capped at $k \in \{1, 2\}$ for `Heart` and `Diabetes`). Under `positivity="conical"`, `{python} N.us_n_conical_conv` of `{python} N.us_n_conical_fits` fits converge with maximum Gram defect $D(\mathbf{V}_m) \le$ `{python} N.us_conical_max_defect` and maximum inter-column cosine `{python} N.us_conical_max_cos`. Under radial simplex `positivity="convex"`, `{python} N.us_n_convex_conv` of `{python} N.us_n_convex_fits` fits converge with maximum inter-column cosine `{python} N.us_convex_max_cos` and maximum Gram defect `{python} N.us_convex_max_defect` (non-zero defect arises because radial $\ell_1$-simplex columns have unequal $\ell_2$ norms when disjoint support sizes differ). The three non-converged `convex` fits are all on `Diabetes` ($p = [5, 5]$) at $k = 2$ (`Stop_Reason = "no_descent"` across seeds `42, 43, 44`, consensus `{python} N.us_diab_cvx_u`, linear `{python} N.us_diab_cvx_lin`), whereas `positivity="conical"` converges in all $3/3$ splits with consensus `{python} N.us_diab_con_u`, linear `{python} N.us_diab_con_lin`, and Gram defect `{python} N.us_diab_con_defect`. Pooled across cohorts for `conical`, mean consensus score rises from `{python} N.us_con_k1_u` ($k = 1$, linear `{python} N.us_con_k1_lin`) to `{python} N.us_con_k2_u` ($k = 2$, linear `{python} N.us_con_k2_lin`) and `{python} N.us_con_k3_u` ($k = 3$, linear `{python} N.us_con_k3_lin`). At each cohort's target rank ($k = 2$ for `Heart` and `Diabetes`, $k = 3$ for `ADNI-MCI`, `MultiOmics`, `TCGA-KIRC`, and `mfeat`), `fit_uniform_shrunk` (`conical`) reaches linear scores of `{python} N.us_brca_con_lin` (`MultiOmics`), `{python} N.us_mfeat_con_lin` (`mfeat`), `{python} N.us_heart_con_lin` (`Heart`), `{python} N.us_kirc_con_lin` (`TCGA-KIRC`), `{python} N.us_diab_con_lin` (`Diabetes`), and `{python} N.us_adni_con_lin` (`ADNI-MCI`).

(A) Target-rank out-of-sample linear probe (`XV`, bars) and consensus (`U`, open circles) scores across cohorts (`k = 2` for `Heart` and `Diabetes`, `k = 3` otherwise) comparing Part A best `simlr` against Part B `conical` and `convex`. (B) Normalized Gram defect $D(\\mathbf{V}_m)$ on a log scale across cohorts (maximum inter-column cosine `0.000` for both Part B regimes is reported in the panel title and @tbl-v043-part-b)."
#| out-width: 100%
#| echo: false
import os
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from pysimlr.plotting import theme, VIEW_COLORS

csv_pa_raw = "results_cache/part_a_simlr_v043_raw.csv"
if not os.path.exists(csv_pa_raw):
    csv_pa_raw = "paper/results_cache/part_a_simlr_v043_raw.csv"
csv_pb = "results_cache/part_b_uniform_shrunk_summary.csv"
if not os.path.exists(csv_pb):
    csv_pb = "paper/results_cache/part_b_uniform_shrunk_summary.csv"

df_pa_raw = pd.read_csv(csv_pa_raw)
df_pb = pd.read_csv(csv_pb)

cohorts = ["ADNI-MCI", "MultiOmics", "TCGA-KIRC", "Heart", "Diabetes", "mfeat"]
target_k = {"ADNI-MCI": 3, "MultiOmics": 3, "TCGA-KIRC": 3, "Heart": 2, "Diabetes": 2, "mfeat": 3}

pa_lin, pa_u, pa_def = [], [], []
con_lin, con_u, con_def = [], [], []
cvx_lin, cvx_u, cvx_def = [], [], []
for ds in cohorts:
    sub_a = df_pa_raw[df_pa_raw["Dataset"] == ds].groupby(["Positivity", "Sparseness_Target"], dropna=False)[["Strictly_Linear_Metric", "Predictive_Metric", "Frame_Defect_D"]].mean()
    best_idx = sub_a["Strictly_Linear_Metric"].idxmax()
    pa_lin.append(float(sub_a.loc[best_idx, "Strictly_Linear_Metric"]))
    pa_u.append(float(sub_a.loc[best_idx, "Predictive_Metric"]))
    pa_def.append(float(sub_a.loc[best_idx, "Frame_Defect_D"]))

    tk = target_k[ds]
    rc = df_pb[(df_pb["Dataset"] == ds) & (df_pb["Positivity"] == "conical") & (df_pb["k"] == tk)].iloc[0]
    rv = df_pb[(df_pb["Dataset"] == ds) & (df_pb["Positivity"] == "convex") & (df_pb["k"] == tk)].iloc[0]
    con_lin.append(float(rc["US_Lin"]))
    con_u.append(float(rc["US_Metric"]))
    con_def.append(max(float(rc["US_Defect"]), 1e-16))
    cvx_lin.append(float(rv["US_Lin"]))
    cvx_u.append(float(rv["US_Metric"]))
    cvx_def.append(max(float(rv["US_Defect"]), 1e-16))

with theme():
    fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12.0, 4.2), dpi=200, constrained_layout=True)
    x = np.arange(len(cohorts))
    w = 0.25

    ax1.bar(x - w, pa_lin, w, color=VIEW_COLORS[0], label="Part A best simlr (XV)")
    ax1.bar(x, con_lin, w, color=VIEW_COLORS[1], label="Part B conical (XV)")
    ax1.bar(x + w, cvx_lin, w, color=VIEW_COLORS[2], label="Part B convex (XV)")
    ax1.scatter(x - w, pa_u, facecolor="#fcfcfb", edgecolor=VIEW_COLORS[0], s=32, lw=1.4, zorder=4, label="Consensus U (open)")
    ax1.scatter(x, con_u, facecolor="#fcfcfb", edgecolor=VIEW_COLORS[1], s=32, lw=1.4, zorder=4)
    ax1.scatter(x + w, cvx_u, facecolor="#fcfcfb", edgecolor=VIEW_COLORS[2], s=32, lw=1.4, zorder=4)
    ax1.set_xticks(x)
    ax1.set_xticklabels(cohorts, fontsize=8.2)
    ax1.set_ylim(0.0, 1.05)
    ax1.set_ylabel(r"Out-of-sample score ($\uparrow$)")
    ax1.set_title("A. Target-rank linear XV and consensus U")
    ax1.grid(True, axis="y")
    ax1.legend(loc="upper left", fontsize=7.6, ncol=2)

    ax2.bar(x - w, pa_def, w, color=VIEW_COLORS[0], label="Part A best simlr D(V)")
    ax2.bar(x, con_def, w, color=VIEW_COLORS[1], label="Part B conical D(V)")
    ax2.bar(x + w, cvx_def, w, color=VIEW_COLORS[2], label="Part B convex D(V)")
    ax2.set_yscale("log")
    ax2.set_ylim(1e-16, 40.0)
    ax2.set_xticks(x)
    ax2.set_xticklabels(cohorts, fontsize=8.2)
    ax2.set_ylabel(r"Gram defect D(V) (log scale, $\downarrow$)")
    ax2.set_title("B. Orthogonality defect across cohorts (max cos = 0.000)")
    ax2.grid(True, axis="y")
    ax2.legend(loc="upper center", ncol=3, fontsize=7.2)

    plt.show()
```
